case_studies.title: Design Conductor 2.0: An agent builds a TurboQuant inference accelerator in 80 hours
case_studies.abstract: Driven by a rapid co-evolution of both harness and underlying models, LLM agents are improving at a dizzying pace. In our prior work (performed in Dec. 2025), we introduced "Design Conductor" (or just "Conductor"), a system capable of building a 5-stage Linux-capable RISC-V CPU in 12 hours. In this work, we introduce an updated multi-agent harness powered by frontier models released in April 2026, which is able to handle 80x larger tasks, at higher quality, fully autonomously. Following a brief introduction, we examine 4 designs that the system produced autonomously, including "VerTQ", an LLM
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of rapidly building complex inference accelerators by introducing Design Conductor 2.0, a system that can build a TurboQuant inference accelerator in 80 hours. The team built an updated multi-agent harness powered by frontier models, which can handle 80x larger tasks at higher quality. The result is a fully autonomous system that can produce high-quality designs, including the VerTQ LLM accelerator.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI or machine learning infrastructure, here is what to do: monitor the development of Design Conductor 2.0, assess its potential to accelerate your AI workflows, and consider evaluating its autonomous design capabilities. This flags a risk: if your org uses custom-built accelerators, check your design workflows for potential optimization opportunities. Not directly applicable to general cloud infrastructure work, but relevant to AI and ML teams.
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper presents a significant advancement in AI-powered design automation, demonstrating the ability to build complex systems like TurboQuant inference accelerators in a short period. The use of a multi-agent harness and frontier models showcases innovative applications of LLMs in IT infrastructure and software engineering.

case_studies.title: Continual Knowledge Updating in LLM Systems: Learning Through Multi-Timescale Memory Dynamics
case_studies.abstract: LLMs are trained once, then deployed into a world that never stops changing. External memory compensates for this, but most systems manage it explicitly rather than letting it adapt on its own. Biological memory works differently: coupled multi-timescale dynamics make new associations immediately usable, strengthen what repetition confirms, and let the rest fade. We argue that external memory should follow a similar principle. In Memini, this view takes the form of an associative memory that organizes knowledge as a directed graph. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of outdated knowledge in large language models by creating a system called Memini, which uses a dynamic memory approach to update knowledge over time. Memini builds an associative memory that organizes knowledge as a directed graph, allowing it to adapt to changing information. The result is a more efficient and effective way to manage knowledge in language models.

This could have implications for IT engineers working with LLM APIs and MLOps. The idea of an associative memory that organizes knowledge as a directed graph is interesting and potentially relevant to IT infrastructure. However, the paper's focus is more on the theoretical aspects, and its immediate applicability to real-world IT problems is limited.

case_studies.title: Executable World Models for ARC-AGI-3 in the Era of Coding Agents
case_studies.abstract: We evaluate an initial coding-agent system for ARC-AGI-3 in which the agent maintains an executable Python world model, verifies it against previous observations, refactors it toward simpler abstractions as a practical proxy for an MDL-like simplicity bias, and plans through the model before acting. The system is intentionally direct: it uses a scripted controller, predefined world-model interfaces, verifier programs, and a plan executor, but no hand-coded game-specific logic. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of creating a coding-agent system that can learn and adapt to new environments, the authors built a system that maintains an executable world model and refactors it for simplicity, the result is a system that can play 25 public games with no hand-coded game-specific logic. The system uses a scripted controller and predefined interfaces to verify and plan actions. This research is focused on artificial intelligence and not directly relevant to cloud infrastructure management.
